title: Define Acceptance Orbits: PRD handshake + rollback playbook
creator: Lina Morales
description: Purpose: Create a lightweight, repeatable "Acceptance Orbits" playbook that standardizes how PRDs travel through Engineering, Design, and Legal for signoff, and defines a minimal rollback/remediation procedure when acceptance criteria are not met. This ticket produces two artifacts: (1) an "Acceptance Map" template (Confluence) with lane-level owners, TTLs, and gating criteria; (2) a compact rollback/remediation ledger template and escalation flow tied to the PRD review step.
scope: Includes: drafting the Acceptance Map template, defining per-stakeholder TTLs and required artifacts, an example filled map for the 'Private Upgrade' PRD, a rollback playbook with owner roles and automation hooks, and a written handoff checklist for PMs. Excludes: implementing automation in the Console or Linear. Implementation tickets will be split out after acceptance.
deliverables: Confluence: Acceptance Map template with example
One-pager PRD review checklist for PMs
Runbook for escalation and emergency rollback (owner + contact)
acceptance_criteria: Acceptance Map template exists in Confluence and includes discrete lanes for Eng/Design/Legal with signoff checkboxes
Each lane includes a TTL (default 3 business days) and an explicit list of required artifacts (design comps, security questionnaire, integration tests)
Rollback playbook includes clear rollback triggers, owner assignment, and a communication template for customers/internal teams
Example Acceptance Map is filled for the 'Private Upgrade' PRD and has signoff from at least one eng lead, one design lead, and Legal counsel
A short training note (1 page) is attached and shared to the PRD author guide
updates: 2026-03-03: Kickoff meeting with Eng (Marco Alvarez), Design (Priya Nair), Legal (S. Gupta). Agreed to 3 business day TTLs as default and 24-hour escalate window for high-severity customer-impact blockers.
2026-03-05: Draft Acceptance Map posted to Confluence (link placeholder). Design requested accessibility checklist inclusion; added as artifact requirement for design lane.
2026-03-07: Legal reviewed data residency language; asked for optional KMS/HSM approval step for Private deployments. Marked as conditional artifact in Acceptance Map.

2026-03-10: Engineering asked for integration test definition and canary criteria to be mandatory for runtime-impacting PRDs (tagged in template). Decided to surface 'runtime-impact' toggle in PRD authoring flow.
2026-03-12: Filled example for 'Private Upgrade' PRD and routed to stakeholders for dry-run signoff. Minor wording tweaks requested by Design and Legal. Preparing one-pager training note.
risks_and_tradeoffs: Stricter gating reduces review rework but increases up-front latency for PRD approvals
3-day TTL is a compromise; for high-priority enterprise deals, explicit expedited lanes will be used (separate process)
Manual ledger is simplest to start; automation (Linear custom fields / Console hooks) is future work and will require engineering effort
notes: Example PRD: PM-7012 Private Upgrade (used as canonical example)
Proposed escalation: PM -> Eng lead -> Head of Platform -> Legal Counsel on call
next_steps: Finalize Acceptance Map text and circulate for signoff by 2026-03-16
Create one-pager training note and embed in PRD authoring template
Spin up follow-on engineering ticket to add Linear custom fields for 'Acceptance TTL' and 'Acceptance Ledger' if stakeholders adopt the template
